gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Expressive from the first glance, Revalia strides along with widely separated letters and an open-bottomed g. Noto Sans Myanmar follows with a heavy-looking, clean strip of text, its c opening broadly.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Revalia's lowercase g leaves its lower curve open, and its widely spaced letters give the heading a relaxed, bold stride. Noto Sans Nabataean keeps lowercase nearly cap-height, so paragraphs feel dense yet open.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Revalia is the loud one, a bold display face whose letters stroll apart and whose g stays open below. Noto Sans Nushu does the quiet work, a sans-serif with towering lowercase and terminals held away from the stroke.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Clean and contemporary, Noto Sans Ogham has wide gaps in its e and lowercase that looks surprisingly bold. Revalia handles the expressive display moments, while this one carries the text.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-old-hungaria: Noto Sans Old Hungarian reads approachable, with big open counters that hold up at tiny sizes. Revalia adds bold, expressive swagger above it, and that loose, stretched-out heading against such friendly text is the pair's real charm.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Noto Sans Old Italic reads contemporary and businesslike, with lowercase almost as high as its capitals and curve endings kept apart. Revalia handles the bold, expressive display work; this one handles the text.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-old-north-ar: Revalia's open-bottomed g gives it away at once. Noto Sans Old North Arabian is dense and approachable with outward-pointing terminals, and next to the loose, bold heading it feels grounded.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdian: Revalia's relaxed stride, with widely separated letters and an open-curved g, makes the heading feel bold and expressive. Noto Sans Old Sogdian answers with a clean, approachable body whose wide-mouthed letters stay crisp even when shrunk.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-noto-sans-old-turkic: Revalia lets its g hang open at the bottom while widely separated letters stroll across a bold, expressive line. Noto Sans Old Turkic gives the pair its approachable side, with chunky lowercase and open-mouthed curves that stay clear.
